effects: The signer sends msg.value ETH, which the contract stakes into Lido stETH via submit(_referral).
The contract wraps the minted stETH into wstETH and transfers all of that wstETH to the signer (msg.sender). The amount depends on Lido's share rate, and there is no minimum.
The referral address gets credit in Lido's referral event only. No signer assets go to it.
formats.shown: "Stake 15.49 ETH" with an 'Amount to stake' field. Nothing says that wstETH (not stETH) comes back, and the referral is hidden.

findings.title: stakeETH: the screen never says the signer receives wstETH. The reader expected stETH.
findings.evidence: WstethStaker.sol stakeETH: `uint256 wstETHAmount = wstETH.wrap(stethAmount); wstETH.transfer(msg.sender, wstETHAmount);`. Descriptor intent "Stake ETH" / "Stake {@.value}" has no mention of wstETH. Case 0 mined: 12.597855047834535196 WSTETH in to the signer. The reader wrote "normally stETH of about 15.49".
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Stake ETH for wstETH" and the interpolatedIntent to "Stake {@.value} and receive wstETH". A label or a message could also say the wstETH amount follows the Lido exchange rate.

findings.title: stakeETH: the wstETH amount comes from Lido's share rate, has no minimum and is not in calldata.
findings.evidence: WstethStaker.sol _getPooledEthBySharesRoundUp reads stETH.getTotalPooledEther()/getTotalShares(). wrap() decides the amount. There is no minOut parameter. In case 0, 15.49 ETH became 12.5979 wstETH.
findings.fix: No field can show it. The intent can name the asset received.

cases.notes: The 15.49 ETH sent is shown correctly. 12.5979 wstETH arrived, but the screen names no asset received, and the reader expected about 15.49 stETH.

stakeETH(address _referral).worst: stakeETH: the screen never says the signer receives wstETH. The reader expected stETH.
